picks.name: three.js Sky.js + Water.js (examples/jsm/objects)
picks.licenseEvidence: From mrdoob/three.js LICENSE (root of repo): 'The MIT License ... Permission is hereby granted, free of charge, to any person obtaining a copy of this software ... THE SOFTWARE IS PROVIDED "AS IS", WITHOUT WARRANTY OF ANY KIND'
picks.gives: Procedural physical sky dome (Preetham/Rayleigh-Mie atmospheric scattering driven by sun elevation/azimuth, so day-night is just animating one parameter) plus a reflective/refracted water-plane shader with normal-map distortion and Fresnel — both are self-contained ~300-line modules, no external dep…
picks.where: T40 'Enter the OASIS' scene: skydome + sun/day-night driver, and any water plane in the low-poly world
picks.risk: Water.js explicitly only supports WebGLRenderer, not WebGPURenderer — confirm renderer choice before committing. Addon APIs shift between three.js minor versions, so pin the exact tag when vendoring and re-check on upgrade.

picks.name: THREE.Terrain
picks.licenseEvidence: From LICENSE.txt on gh-pages branch (quoted by fetch): 'The MIT License ... Permission is hereby granted, free of charge, to any person obtaining a copy of this software and associated documentation files ... to deal in the Software without restriction ...'
picks.gives: Procedural heightmap-based low-poly terrain generation for Three.js (multiple noise/diamond-square algorithms, seeded randomness, instanced scattered decoration meshes, a grass-generation module) — purpose-built for exactly the 'low-poly terrain' part of the goal.
picks.where: T40 low-poly terrain generation in the Enter-the-OASIS world
picks.risk: Small single-maintainer project (905 stars) with an unusual default branch (gh-pages) — verify the pinned three.js peer version (currently tracks 0.186.0, matching the Sky/Water pick) stays compatible on upgrade. rejected.name: Low Poly City Pack (owlora, itch.io)
rejected.reason: Page states a custom 'free to use for personal and commercial projects' phrase with no LICENSE file and no standard OSI/CC designation — unverifiable, non-standard license, not in the allowed list (MIT/Apache-2.0/BSD/CC0/CC-BY).

top: three.js's own Sky.js/Water.js addons (MIT, r186) give the physical sky + water shaders for free since three is already the runtime dependency.
Kenney's City Kit (CC0, via the shorepine/kenney mirror) supplies ready-to-load low-poly glTF buildings well under the 2MB asset cap.
THREE.Terrain (MIT, v3.1.1, active) is a small, focused, still-maintained library that directly covers the low-poly terrain-generation gap.
moved: Kenney City Kit (Commercial + Suburban), via shorepine/kenney mirror
goal: Low-poly world and sky for the later Enter-the-OASIS Three.js scene: procedural/physical sky shaders, low-poly terrain/city/buildings, stylized water, day-night
